sentences.text: 2. Having heard Mr. V. Sambasiva Rao, learned counsel for the Appellant/insurance company and Mr. V. Atchuta Rao, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants, perused the entire material on record.

3. The claim petition was filed under Section 166 of M.V Act seeking compensation of Rs.4,00,000/-
for the death of deceased in Motor accident.
The case of the insurance company is that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving license and as per the evidence adduced by them the license was valid up to 17.04.2004.

3. Learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that the court below without considering the evidence on record has held that the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and liberty is granted to the insurance company to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

The Court below has considered the evidence of RW.2, who is Administrative officer in D.T.C.
Ranga Reddy, according to whom, the accident took place on 22.07.2005 and the driving license was valid up to 17.04.2004.
The court below has observed that even as per the own evidence of RW2, the driving license can be renewed at any place throughout India and he may not be having information about renewal of the same.
Having considered so, the Court below has granted the compensation by applying the principle of pay and recover.
5. According to the appeal of the appellant/insurance company, they are not liable to pay the compensation and hence question of pay and recover will not arise.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Swaran Singh1, the order passed by the court below is a well considered one and this Court finds no reasons to interfere with the The United India Insurance Company ... vs N.
